summary: This work develops reinforcement learning techniques for large language models that improve reasoning performance while reducing response length, through methods that enable finer-grained control over token generation during training.

Both works propose reinforcement learning frameworks that enhance large language model reasoning capabilities through self-generated rewards without relying on external human supervision, demonstrating competitive performance on reasoning and mathematical tasks.

This work develops reinforcement learning algorithms for improving large language model reasoning on mathematical tasks, with approaches that either reduce computational overhead through selective data sampling or provide theoretical guarantees through value-based learning.

This work investigates how reinforcement learning can elicit meta-thinking and reasoning capabilities in large language models, demonstrating that multi-agent and model-free RL approaches enable LLMs to develop internal reasoning processes that improve performance on complex tasks.

This work addresses data-driven challenges in scaling reinforcement learning from human feedback for large language models, proposing methods to improve reward assessment and handle tasks with complex or difficult-to-verify ground truth solutions.

This work investigates reinforcement learning-based training methods for improving large language model reasoning capabilities, proposing novel token-level optimization approaches that enhance solution quality while addressing challenges that emerge during RL fine-tuning.

Both works apply reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to improve large language models' ability to generate executable outputs in specialized domains, where the models learn to self-correct through interaction with automated verification mechanisms without relying solely on ground-truth supervision.

This work analyzes limitations of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for reinforcement learning of large language models on reasoning tasks and proposes improved methods that address gradient-based training issues to enhance performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

Both works develop Process Reward Models (PRMs) that provide step-level evaluations to supervise intermediate reasoning in large language models, with applications to complex reasoning tasks, and demonstrate that their approaches can achieve competitive or superior performance compared to strong baselines while reducing computational or annotation costs.

This work develops reinforcement learning algorithms for improving large language model reasoning that eliminate the need for critic networks and operate efficiently with minimal generations per prompt, achieving competitive performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks while reducing computational overhead compared to policy-based baselines.

Both works propose novel fine-tuning strategies for large language models that improve reasoning performance by focusing on critical components within the reasoning process, rather than treating entire reasoning trajectories uniformly.

This work investigates the effectiveness of reinforcement learning approaches for enhancing reasoning capabilities in large language models, examining whether RL training genuinely elicits novel reasoning abilities or primarily optimizes sampling efficiency within the base model's existing capacity across mathematical and problem-solving tasks.

This work develops reinforcement learning methods for improving reasoning capabilities of large language models using unlabeled or limited data, employing majority voting mechanisms to estimate rewards without access to ground-truth labels.

This work develops methods to improve large language model reasoning by training verifier or critic models through reinforcement learning and adversarial interactions, eliminating the need for manual step-level annotations and demonstrating enhanced performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

Both works address the limitation of on-policy reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for training large reasoning models, proposing frameworks that augment on-policy approaches with additional guidance—either off-policy demonstrations or self-generated explanations conditioned on ground truth—to enable models to explore reasoning trajectories beyond their initial capabilities and improve performance on complex mathematical reasoning tasks.

This work develops reinforcement learning frameworks to enhance reasoning capabilities in diffusion language models, demonstrating improvements on mathematical and code generation tasks through optimized intermediate generation steps.

Both works propose methods for improving reasoning capabilities in large language models through self-improvement mechanisms that reduce reliance on expensive external supervision, achieving performance gains across multiple benchmarks while enhancing training efficiency.

Both works propose unsupervised or self-directed methods to enhance the reasoning capabilities of large language models without relying on external supervision, achieving competitive performance improvements on mathematical and reasoning benchmarks.

This work addresses the challenge of training language models to perform complex reasoning in specialized domains by combining supervised fine-tuning with expert knowledge and reinforcement learning, enabling models to achieve strong performance on tasks where standard approaches struggle.

This work develops reinforcement learning frameworks that improve large language models' reasoning capabilities through scalable task construction with verifiable rewards and curriculum-based training strategies.

This work develops reinforcement learning frameworks that train Large Language Models to simultaneously improve their problem-solving and self-verification abilities for complex reasoning tasks, enabling effective test-time scaling on mathematical reasoning benchmarks without relying on external verifiers.

Both works propose algorithmic improvements to reinforcement learning methods for enhancing Large Language Model reasoning capabilities, addressing optimization challenges in policy gradient-based training through novel modifications to the reward or sampling mechanisms.

This work applies large-scale reinforcement learning to enhance mathematical and code reasoning capabilities in language models, demonstrating that RL training with outcome-based rewards improves performance on math and code benchmarks while eliciting and extending the models' reasoning abilities beyond those achieved through supervised fine-tuning alone.

This work investigates how token entropy patterns influence reinforcement learning approaches for improving Large Language Model reasoning, demonstrating that entropy-based optimization of critical decision tokens can enhance performance on challenging mathematical and reasoning tasks without requiring extensive labeled data.

Both studies address the challenge of improving the effectiveness and efficiency of reinforcement learning as a post-training technique for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models, proposing data-centric approaches to optimize RL fine-tuning performance.

This work develops efficient approaches for applying reinforcement learning to improve reasoning capabilities in large language models, addressing the computational challenges of scaling RL training while maintaining or improving model performance on reasoning benchmarks.

This work develops reinforcement learning-based methods to optimize reasoning in large language models, addressing the challenge of efficiently training models to perform complex reasoning tasks through improved gradient estimation and hybrid reasoning approaches.

This work investigates how reinforcement learning enhances mathematical reasoning and complex problem-solving in large language models beyond surface-level accuracy improvements, revealing that RL enables models to develop novel reasoning strategies and internal approaches that extend beyond the capabilities of base models.

This work investigates reinforcement learning approaches for training language models on mathematical reasoning tasks, demonstrating that leveraging negative samples alongside positive examples in the learning process can improve performance on reasoning benchmarks like MATH.
This work develops reward models that leverage chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time compute to improve the accuracy of reward signals for aligning large language models with human preferences.

Both works propose optimization techniques to improve the training efficiency of reinforcement learning-based reasoning models for large language models, building upon Group Relative Policy Optimization by introducing methods to reduce computational costs while maintaining or improving reasoning performance.

Both works use reinforcement learning to optimize language model reasoning capabilities, with one focusing on adaptive configuration selection across diverse reasoning tasks and the other on training models to generate effective explanations for student distillation, demonstrating improved performance and robustness across different model scales and task distributions.
